P2 · Medium impact · Medium effort — use an additive, trust-gated repository overlay for hard rules. Keep shipped rules authoritative; load a fixed repo-root .sk-git/hard-rules.json only after an operator-owned trust decision keyed to the canonical repository path and remote identity. Never let repository config self-authorize trust or steer the overlay path. Append overlay rules after built-ins; allow only existing GIT_CHECKS and warn severity; require repository-namespaced IDs, reject duplicate IDs against both sets, reject symlinks/path traversal/oversize files, and reject the overlay as a unit on parse/schema/check/ID error without dropping built-ins. Make /doctor:git setup report built-in count, overlay count and one explicit overlay state (absent, active, ignored-untrusted, or invalid), rather than collapsing bad/missing overlay input into a healthy empty set. This tightens the earlier additive-overlay proposal: the current dispatch reader loads one sibling file, fail-opens to an empty list on read/parse/shape errors, skips unknown checks, and treats thrown checks as passed; the advisory hook reads the inspected repository's skill path while the setup battery checks only the installed copy.
